channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan and Germany Discuss Expanding Cooperation in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan and Germany held political consultations in Dushanbe on November 13, 2026, to discuss bilateral relations in political, economic, cultural, and other spheres. The talks focused on strengthening cooperation in trade, economy, science, culture, medicine, migration, tourism, and security. Both sides expressed satisfaction with the current level of interaction and interest in further expansion.

item.title: Uzbekistan Agriculture Census Reveals Nearly 1 Million Hectares of Previously Unaccounted Land
item.description: Uzbekistan's first agriculture census has identified nearly 1 million hectares of land not previously reflected in statistical reports. Greenhouse areas were found to be nearly three times larger than previously estimated, while the number of cattle decreased by 2.3 million. The National Statistics Committee presented the final results on November 13.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Georgia Agree to Strengthen Protection for Uzbek Migrants
item.description: Uzbekistan and Georgia have agreed to enhance cooperation on migrant rights and consular assistance. The countries will jointly inform citizens about entry and stay regulations. This agreement follows discussions between Uzbekistan's Deputy Foreign Minister and Georgia's Ambassador, focusing on protecting Uzbek citizens in Georgia.

item.title: Abu Dhabi Talks: Russia and Ukraine Agree on Prisoner Exchange, Not Peace
item.description: Recent talks in Abu Dhabi, mediated by the US, saw Russia and Ukraine agree on a large-scale prisoner exchange but failed to resolve core disagreements on occupied territories and future security. Russia seeks a comprehensive agreement on European security, while Ukraine emphasizes ending the war and guaranteeing its security.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 2027 State Budget to Maintain Social Focus, Exceeding Expenditures Over Revenues
item.description: Uzbekistan's economy is projected to grow by at least 8% this year, with GDP exceeding $200 billion. The 2027 state budget will retain its social orientation, allocating significant funds to education and healthcare. The plan aims for sustained economic growth and increased per capita income by 2030 and beyond.

item.title: Jeti-Oguz District Industrial Output Reaches 128.5 Billion Som
item.description: Industrial production in Kyrgyzstan's Jeti-Oguz district grew from 71.1 billion som in 2021 to 128.5 billion som in 2025, including output from the Kumtor mine. The district's total investment is projected at 21.4 billion som. Projects include drinking water initiatives and 81 bridges, with plans for a ski base and tourism development.

item.title: Kabul Women Recount Fear of Taliban Harassment and Interrogation
item.description: Kabul residents report increased harassment of women by Taliban intelligence and Morality Police, confining girls to homes and restricting their societal participation. This treatment, often by plain-clothed individuals, reportedly enables personal abuse and fosters widespread fear. A resident described daily interrogations by authorities, particularly when traveling alone.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: Old Rivals and New Faces Vie for Office
item.description: Eleven individuals have declared their intention to run in Kyrgyzstan's presidential election, broadly categorized into three groups: past rivals of current President Sadyr Japarov, political figures critical of the government, and newcomers to the political arena. Among them are businessman Aimen Kasenov, former MP Baktybek Kalmametov, and ex-Constitutional Chamber judge Klara Sooronkulova.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Transport Minister Reports Progress on China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway
item.description: The construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is progressing rapidly, according to Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Transport and Communications, Talantbek Soltobaev. The project, planned for five years with completion by 2031, involves extensive tunnel work and infrastructure development. Over 10,000 workers and 7,000 units of special equipment are currently engaged.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Complete Two Nuclear Power Plants by 2035
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to complete the construction of two nuclear power plants, "Balkhash" and "Moynkum," by 2035. The "Balkhash" plant will be built with Russian "Rosatom," while negotiations for the "Moynkum" plant are underway with China's CNNC. The government aims to accelerate preparation for these projects.

item.title: Taliban Ban Male Doctors from Treating Women in Parts of Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban's ban on male doctors examining and treating female patients in parts of Afghanistan is making healthcare access difficult for women. In areas without female doctors, women are deprived of medical services, forced to endure pain or travel for treatment. The Taliban has warned doctors of arrest if they defy the order.

item.title: Sweden Interested in Recruiting Uzbeks for Healthcare and Agriculture Sectors
item.description: Sweden has expressed interest in recruiting citizens from Uzbekistan for its healthcare and agriculture sectors. Discussions were held regarding the training and employment of Uzbek nurses in areas facing labor shortages. This initiative aims to address staffing needs in specific regions of Sweden.

item.title: Turkmenistan Advocates for Global Cooperation on Climate Change at COP31 Summit
item.description: Turkmenistan's National Leader, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, addressed the COP31 Summit, emphasizing global cooperation to combat climate change. He highlighted Turkmenistan's commitment to international climate agreements and its National Climate Strategy, including measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and enhance energy efficiency.

item.title: Tourism in Ton District, Issyk-Kul Region, Increases 14-Fold in Five Years
item.description: Tourist numbers in Ton district, Issyk-Kul region, surged by 14 times compared to 2021, exceeding 73,000 in 2026. The district now has 41 tourist facilities, creating 195 permanent and 5,000 seasonal jobs. Tax revenues from tourism reached 18.1 million soms in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Man Arrested in Almaty for Allegedly Collecting Over 60 Million Tenge via Telegram
item.description: A 44-year-old man has been arrested in Almaty on suspicion of promoting religious extremism through closed Telegram groups while residing abroad. According to investigators, he collected over 60 million tenge from his followers. Some of his audio lectures were previously deemed extremist materials by a court.

item.title: Tajikistan and Russia Discuss Energy Sector Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with the Director General of Russia's Inter RAO in Moscow to discuss energy cooperation. Key topics included the operation of the Sangtuda-1 HPP and prospects for joint projects. Both sides expressed readiness to continue fruitful cooperation and strengthen mutually beneficial relations in the energy sector.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Reviews Socio-Economic Development in Issyk-Kul Regions
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited the Jet-Oguz and Ton districts of the Issyk-Kul region to review their socio-economic development. Industrial production in Jet-Oguz increased significantly, with investments projected at 21.4 billion soms. Road repairs, bridge construction, and drinking water projects are underway. The Ton district also saw a 5.1-fold increase in industrial output.

item.title: Armenia Loses Voting Rights in CSTO Amidst Broadened Cooperation with US and Neighbors
item.description: Armenia has been stripped of its voting rights in the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) due to unpaid membership dues, though it retains its membership. Concurrently, Yerevan is expanding cooperation with Turkey, Azerbaijan, the US, and European countries. Prime Minister Pashinyan met with Turkish President Erdoğan and Azerbaijani President Aliyev during recent summits.

item.title: Over 575,000 People in Kazakhstan Diagnosed with Diabetes, Ministry Reports
item.description: As of October 1, 2026, Kazakhstan has registered over 575,000 individuals with diabetes, including more than 30,987 cases of type 1 diabetes, according to the Ministry of Health. Screening programs have been expanded to detect the disease early, with over 1.6 million people screened in the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan's TOUR TJ Startup Named Best in TravelTech at World Tourism Awards 2026
item.description: Tajikistan's technology startup TOUR TJ won the Best TravelTech Startup 2026 award at the World Tourism Awards ceremony in Brussels. Founder and CEO Idibek Vokhidov accepted the award, highlighting the achievement as significant for the team and for Tajikistan's tourism and IT sectors, demonstrating the potential of local startups on the global stage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Free Diabetes Screening for Citizens Aged 40-76
item.description: Kazakhstan has expanded free diabetes screening to citizens aged 40 to 76. Eligible individuals can now undergo tests for glycated hemoglobin, triglycerides, and low-density lipoproteins every two years. The Ministry of Health also noted increased provision of insulin pumps and supplies for specific patient groups.

item.title: SIBUR Under Sanctions: Expert Discusses Implications for Kazakhstan's Petrochemical Projects
item.description: The UK has sanctioned Russia's SIBUR Holding, raising concerns for Kazakhstan. Expert Olzhas Baidildinov notes SIBUR's significant stakes in KPI (polypropylene) and the upcoming 'Sillen' polyethylene plant. Risks include financing, technology, and equipment procurement for 'Sillen', though KPI's China-focused sales may be less affected.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov Reviews Socio-Economic Development in Issyk-Kul Region's Districts
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited the Je t i-Ogüz and Tong districts of the Issyk-Kul region to review their socio-economic development plans for 2021-2026. He was briefed on industrial growth, infrastructure improvements, and ongoing investment projects, including tourism development.

item.title: UNHCR Representative Calls for Sustained International Support for Afghanistan
item.description: The UNHCR representative in Afghanistan urged the international community to continue its support, citing the significant pressure on the country from over 6.5 million Afghan returnees in three years. Arafat Jamal highlighted challenges like poverty, drought, and climate disasters facing returnees, noting their influx strains Afghanistan's economy and humanitarian resources. He also emphasized that stability in Afghanistan is a global concern due to its strategic location.

item.title: International tribunal rejects Turkish investors' claims against Uzbekistan
item.description: An international arbitration tribunal at the ICSID has rejected all claims filed by Turkish citizen Mehmet Zeki Obuz and others against Uzbekistan. The ruling concluded a five-year legal dispute related to the food industry. Uzbekistan's interests were represented by the Ministry of Justice and an international law firm.

item.title: Tajikistan and UNODC Discuss Cooperation on Combating Human Trafficking
item.description: Tajikistan's First Deputy Interior Minister met with the UNODC regional representative to discuss strengthening cooperation in preventing human trafficking and protecting victims' rights. They explored enhancing professional skills of officials and strengthening relevant structures. The discussion also covered modern threats like domestic violence and the need for coordinated action with international partners.

item.title: Russia Seeks Regional Control Over Afghanistan Amidst Shifting Global Dynamics
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov advocates for regional nations to manage Afghanistan's affairs, citing Western failures. Moscow aims to limit Western influence, support the Taliban, and expand its own political, security, and economic reach in Central Asia and Afghanistan. The Taliban's return has made Afghanistan a key regional security concern, with ongoing issues of armed groups, drug trafficking, extremism, and crises.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Decline for Second Consecutive Week Amid Market Concerns
item.description: Global oil prices, including Brent and WTI, have fallen for the second consecutive week, with both benchmarks decreasing by approximately 2.5%. This decline is attributed to increased supply and weakening global demand, further influenced by a report from the International Energy Agency. US inventory data also contributed to the price drop.

item.title: Mountain Nations Fail to Include Glacier Melting on COP31 Agenda
item.description: Mountain countries, including Kyrgyzstan, Nepal, and Bhutan, were unsuccessful in getting the issue of melting glaciers officially added to the COP31 agenda. This marks the fourth consecutive failed attempt by these nations to secure a separate discussion on glaciers within UN climate talks. Major countries and the EU reportedly blocked the initiative, fearing new environmental protection financial obligations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service Publishes Average Monthly Salaries for 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service has released the average monthly salary (SMZ) figures for 2027, which will be used for calculating income tax and insurance contributions. The nationwide average has increased by 17.9% to 42,493 soms. These new figures, applicable from January 1, 2027, will be used in legally stipulated cases, with specific rates set for each district and city.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Transfer Up to 30% of Pension Assets to Private Managers by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to significantly reform its pension asset management system, aiming to transfer 20-30% of pension assets to private investment companies by 2030. This initiative, part of the Capital Market Development Program, seeks to provide long-term financing for the national economy. Currently, nearly 99% of pension savings are managed by the National Bank.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans State Funding for Liver Transplant Surgeries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to include liver transplant surgeries in the list of high-tech medical services funded by the High-Tech Fund. The Ministry of Health notes a rise in patients with end-stage liver diseases, for whom transplantation is the only radical treatment. The average cost of a transplant is around $17,000.

item.title: ICC Halts Investigation into Alleged Crimes by US Troops in Afghanistan
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has halted its investigation into alleged crimes by US troops in Afghanistan, citing "significant limitations" in carrying out investigations and obtaining evidence. The ruling also ends the probe into alleged crimes by the Islamic State group's affiliate in Khorasan Province. The prosecutor's office has appealed the decision.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Jokes About Appointing Investor's Relative as Mayor
item.description: During a meeting, a resident asked President Sadyr Жапаров for funds to develop the tourist town of Cholpon-Ata. Жапаров joked about appointing an investor's relative as mayor, referencing significant funding provided to another city by an investor named Shirshov. He noted that Cholpon-Ata and Balykchy had already received substantial funding.

item.title: Kandahar Pomegranate Growers Face Economic Hardship Amidst Export Route Closures
item.description: Pomegranate farmers in Afghanistan's Kandahar province are experiencing severe economic difficulties due to closed export routes, particularly with Pakistan, drought, and crop diseases. Prices have dropped by up to 70 percent, failing to cover cultivation costs. Growers report a significant decrease in demand and prices compared to previous years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build Nine Small Hydropower Plants Across Three Regions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct nine small hydropower plants with a total capacity of 108.1 megawatts. These facilities are slated for Talas, Chuy, and Jalal-Abad regions. The Green Energy Fund has launched a tender for land plots to facilitate their construction.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Jizzakh Nuclear Plant to Use Dry Cooling System to Conserve Water
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Oʻzatom" agency states the Jizzakh nuclear power plant will employ a dry cooling system. This technology will dissipate heat using air, avoiding water evaporation. The agency emphasized the importance of not taking water from nature.

item.title: Aqtobe Farmer Detained for 15 Days for Calling Colleagues to Discuss Fuel Prices
item.description: An Aqtobe farmer, Marlen Baimagambetov, was sentenced to 15 days in jail for inviting colleagues to discuss rising diesel fuel prices in a chat group. The court deemed his actions an illegal call for a peaceful assembly, despite his claims of not planning a protest.

item.title: WHO Urges Taliban to Restart House-to-House Polio Vaccinations in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has called on the Taliban to resume house-to-house polio vaccination campaigns in Afghanistan. The organization stated that 25 polio cases were recorded in 2026 and that campaign suspensions hinder reaching all children. Limited female vaccinator participation is also a challenge.

item.title: Bishkek City Council Deputy Taalaibek Zhakypov Detained in Pre-trial Detention Center
item.description: Taalaibek Zhakypov, a deputy of the Bishkek City Council, has been placed in pre-trial detention center No. 1 until December 21. He is suspected of fraud and was initially detained on October 23, 2026, before being released under house arrest.
